correctness.rationale: Affine normalization is possible for each proper quadrilateral. The six unordered vertex differences exhaust the normal constraints; the pair from the diagonals gives the polar bounding square. Exactly one of two opposite-sign and one of two same-sign strips may cut each respective pair of square corners. Cut triangles have exact area δ²/(2ab), are disjoint across sign classes, and multiplication by normalized area 1/2 yields the formula including transition boundaries. Sharp maximum/equality follow from two positive squares, and the infimum/range from Eggleston’s theorem plus a continuous trapezoid path. Independent 148-pair rational half-plane intersection checks agree, but are supplementary only.

value.rationale: Four-vertex polygons are the smallest non-simplicial planar convex polytopes and form a natural two-dimensional affine moduli family. Exact evaluation of the same polar difference-body product central to the polar-Schneider and Makai theories across this entire family, together with its attained image and unique maximizing affine class, supplies a reusable benchmark for extremal and stability questions. The answer is not implied by existing global bounds; no unrestricted convex-body claim is asserted.
